newsitem.title: USA: Wall St bears on the rise, bulls stumble -- survey.
newsitem.headline: Wall St bears on the rise, bulls stumble -- survey.

text.p: Wall Street bears, while still outnumbered, are gaining ground on the bulls, according to a survey of investors taken last week in the midst of a sharp selloff in U.S. stocks.
The survey of 500 investors released on Wednesday by financial services company Quick & Reilly said that 39 percent described themselves as bullish, down from 58 percent in January.
Meanwhile, 31 percent said they were bearish, compared to 20 percent three months ago. Thirty percent described themselves as neutral, compared to 22 percent in January.
The survey was of 500 active investors who are clients of Quick & Reilly. It was conducted by the independent research firm Wirthlin Worldwide and had a sample error of plus or minus 4.5 percent.
Quick & Reilly described the results of the study as showing the prevailing investor mood is "conservatism rather than panic."

It said that 88 percent of investors said a market correction was likely or somewhat likely. But only 12 percent thought the Dow Jones Industrial Average would decline by more than 1,000 points from the 6,500 level.

The Dow was off about 50 points Wednesday afternoon at 6558. The average had risen in the previous three sessions after dropping over 600 points from its record closing high of 7085 March 11 to its close last Thursday at 6477.
Some 39 percent of investors surveyed expected a decline of 500 to 1000 points from the 6,500 level on the Dow, and 47 percent expected a correction of 500 points or less, Quick & Reilly said.
